migrations: MCP v2.1.4 makes production release identity exact: the signed release manifest carries the source Git commit, production propagates and verifies that commit at runtime, the normal MCP build/HTTP surface is strictly tool-only with the compatibility Workbench disabled, the legacy 69-action surface is test-harness-only, and update metadata reports the deployed control profile.
MCP v2.1.3 makes cptr_open_live_workbench explicitly optional so normal ChatGPT Direct Coding starts with the task-relevant tool instead of a Workbench activation prerequisite.

MCP v2.1.2 splits mixed Workbench, SSH, managed Chrome, delegated task, and delegated monitor gateways into read and control surfaces so host safety annotations match capability while destructive/open-world controls remain conservative.
MCP v2.1.1 disables the MCP Apps UI entrypoint: no resources capability is advertised and no tool publishes ui.resourceUri metadata; Workbench session tools remain data-only.
MCP v2.1 adds cptr_workspace_lifecycle for zero-workspace create, clone, import, refresh, archive, and confirmed managed deletion.

The owner-full control profile is the deployment default for fresh installs and upgrades, adding command:external plus confirmed managed-workspace deletion; standard and developer remain explicit opt-down profiles, and legacy full remains an owner-full alias.
Git workspaces warm FDX automatically after provisioning; FDX failure remains a non-fatal fallback to normal CPTR Direct Coding.
Existing CPTR data under ~/.cptr is preserved; Heidi takes a pre-upgrade backup before activation.
FDX protocol 2 remains required for persistent structured resident reads.
